executed_live: Steps 1 to 6 ran for real on 2026-11-03 from 13:01Z to 13:18Z against the app-owning FairPool Sandbox app, with the API and the job worker both on loopback over the local compose database (never the hosted demo one): PAYMENT_ROUTER=single_seller, PAYMENT_MODE=authorize_capture, PAYPAL_APPROVAL_UI=redirect, WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=false, AI_ENABLED=false. A pool was created through POST /api/v1/admin/pools and published, and the worker drove it DRAFT to PUBLISHED to OPEN to RUNNING on its own timers (pool.open, pool.close, pool.seed and pool.allocate all DONE). Three buyers joined through POST /api/v1/intake/manual and POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/entries, each taking a signed entry receipt, and one receipt was read back through the CR-9 route. Two merchants placed four sealed bids through PUT /api/v1/merchant/lots/{lot_id}/bid, each with its receipt hash, and confirmed them inside the window. lot.bid_close and lot.award then decided from those real bids: lot 1 awarded to the 47000-cent merchant with the other bid LOST; on lot 2 that same merchant came back REJECTED with R9_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED because only one of his two declared seats was left after lot 1 and his lot-2 bid declared capacity for two, so lot 2 awarded to the 49000-cent merchant; both lots reached CHECKOUT_OPEN. Three real PayPal Sandbox orders were created (BO-01) -- 5RH40086MG743532T, 8RK07718KJ297035W, 4GW6051813401951B -- each sitting ORDER_CREATED with its offer expiring at 13:44:13Z.
what_this_proves: The two award defects the independent review found are now proved by a running server, not only by tests: the lot_order gate that used to deadlock every lot behind one that had reached checkout, and an R9 failure landing on BS-06 REJECTED with its reason code instead of ELIGIBLE-then-LOST. It also proves the whole auction-to-checkout chain with real bids and a real provider order per seat.
what_this_gate_still_needs: The buyer approval leg of this same scenario: BO-02 from a PayPal approval, then order.authorize, the sweep's capture, one lot reaching FUNDED and the other failing its minimum and voiding to a zero ledger. No live authorization or capture happened in this run.
why_that_leg_is_held: PayPal rendered the checkout for this browser as an India-located guest card flow, and its Sandbox sign-in loads a captcha and would not advance under automation. Our own FR-CK-05 checks restrict the payer country to US (V12), so an India-located approval would be refused by the checks rather than prove anything, and the run was stopped there instead of bending a check. The approval to authorize to capture to refund chain itself is already proven live in IT-5 (C-08, C-09, and the void-to-zero and refund-to-zero ledger runs).
how_to_finish_it: Two ways, both needing the owner. (a) Approve the live orders in a browser before 13:44:13Z by opening http://127.0.0.1:8011/go/<first 8 of the buyer order id> -- a local redirector that sends the browser to the token-bearing approval URL so that URL never enters a log or this file -- signed in as a US Sandbox buyer from a US-located connection, then POST /api/v1/offers/{id}/approved; the server fetches the order, runs the checks, and the worker authorizes and captures. (b) Re-run the same scenario from a US-located connection. The scripts are .tmp/it6_accounts.py, it6_phase1.py, the bid pass and it6_phase3.py; the pool needs open_at in the future and a bid window long enough to place the bids in.
what_is_already_proved_locally: Every leg of IT-6 except the money actually moving: the lot handlers award from real bids and open checkout (test_award_handoff -- the lot_order gate proved both ways after review corrected it to LS-03's 'past BID_CLOSED', since the old AWARDED-or-CANCELLED reading deadlocked every lot behind one that had reached checkout; the ranking tie-break derived from the lot seed and pinned to the published vectors; an R8 or R9 failure landing REJECTED with its reason code; the force-award no-op case), the reconciler sweep captures PENDING authorizations and funds a lot at the MOQ (test_funding, F7, F8), the failure path ends void then refund at a zero ledger (test_failure_path, F9, F24, F10 -- F10 now also proves an aged seat the provider never saw stays locked and is never settled by a write), PT-15 sealing for both a session and an API key, and the buyer UI completing an entry through a signed receipt - driven in a real browser against a live API with the real gateway configured, then re-read from the server after a fresh navigation.
how_to_run: 1. Export PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID, PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET and SINGLE_SELLER_EMAIL for the app-owning FairPool Sandbox app, and set PAYMENT_MODE=authorize_capture, PAYPAL_APPROVAL_UI=redirect, PAYMENT_ROUTER=single_seller, WEBHOOKS_ENABLED per webhook_delivery.json. DONE.
2. Point DATABASE_URL at a migrated local database (alembic upgrade head, currently 0006) and start the API with `make api`. DONE -- run on 127.0.0.1:8010 with the worker beside it.
3. Create one pool with two lots: lot A seats 1 minimum 1, lot B seats 2 minimum 2, entry window short enough to close inside the session, require_paypal_link false. DONE.

4. Two merchants bid through the real path - paste a quote, merchant confirms, reconciliation flags run - so lot.bid_open, lot.bid_close and lot.award decide from real bids and lot.open_checkout opens checkout. No admin force-award. DONE through the structured bid route and confirm; the quote-paste route is the Gemini-quota item below.

5. Buyers join through the buyer UI (Discover -> lobby -> join -> receipt). Joining is free and needs no PayPal approval, so the receipt leg can be completed before any approval happens. DONE through the routes the UI calls.
6. Drain jobs through the registered handlers (no separate worker process is needed locally, which is how IT-5 was run). DONE -- the worker ran the whole lifecycle, reconciler sweep included.
7. Each selected buyer opens their own offer and approves on the PayPal Sandbox page. This is the human step. NOT DONE -- see why_that_leg_is_held.
8. The sweep authorizes, then captures the approved orders; lot A reaches FUNDED when completed captures from distinct buyers meet its minimum.
9. Lot B misses its minimum: authorizations are voided, any completed capture is refunded, and the ledger for that lot nets to zero.

10. Record the provider references (buyer order id, PayPal order/authorization/capture/refund ids, amounts in cents, the resulting lot states and the net ledger) in this file. No token, no client secret and no full approval URL is written here. Order ids, amounts and lot states are in executed_live.
needs_from_owner: PayPal Sandbox buyer approvals: the three US personal buyer accounts (PR1, PR2, PR3 on the personalexample domain) were handed over on 2026-11-03 for this run and their password is held in .env as IT6_BUYER_PASSWORD -- it is not written here, and it should be rotated once the run is finished. The step still needs a human, or a US-located connection, because PayPal's Sandbox sign-in is captcha-gated and our checks refuse a non-US payer.

A Gemini API key with quota for the quote-parsing leg. The free-tier key in .env returns 429, and the quote path refuses with FEATURE_DISABLED rather than pretending to parse; without quota that leg is stated as not executed.

One real webhook delivery for C-15 and webhook_delivery.json. Nothing needs adding: the listener 9WV04847640439813 already exists on the deployed API origin and tracks all seven types. What is missing is a delivery reaching a verifier that is switched on, so it needs either the tunnel pointed at 127.0.0.1:8010 with WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=true, or the deployed app switched to webhooks enabled.
Nothing outstanding on git: the work is merged to `main`, CI is green and the build is deployed.
credential_handling: Sandbox buyer passwords are never written into a file, a log or this repository; the one the owner supplied went into .env as an environment value and the clipboard it passed through was overwritten. Provider references (order, authorization, capture and refund ids) are recorded; tokens, secrets and full approval URLs are not -- the approval URLs were kept out of every artifact by serving them from a local redirector and handing over only the short local path.
fixture_note: The run's admin and merchant accounts are local fixtures made the way tools/demo_seed.py makes its own: IdentityService.register in-process, then the role and the merchant profile with the three R2 attestations. The HTTP register route is the PayPal-first signup path only, so it is not how a fixture account is made. The bid window needed a second attempt because the first fixture pass forgot the merchant role flip and those routes answered 403 until it was set.
